records.title: Public repo still carries 3 credentials marked live in git history (2 Neon owner passwords, 1 Hugging Face token); the HS256 token is closed as not a credential
records.evidenceAtHead: 1) `gh api repos/concept2cure/ClinicalSageAI-2-replit` on 2026-10-13 returned visibility=public, private=false. 2) .gitleaksignore at HEAD still has three `# status: live — revoke (founder; P0-17)` blocks: line 15 (Neon OWNER password, endpoint ep-wild-forest-ahbojhu4, in commits 8d5bce39c/9d1d8d21c/e11adb0c9/eec001307), line 31 (second Neon OWNER password, ep-icy-brook-aha5br78, f457478c8) and line 38 (Hugging Face token, 3e1dcf8f0). 3) The 4th entry, the HS256 token in VaultMarketingPage.jsx, is now `# status: not a secret — closed 2026-10-05` (.gitleaksignore:44-57, commit 8fdfc74bd). Its reasoning holds in code: server/middleware/auth.ts:162 and server/middleware/tenantContext.ts:248 require an access-type token via requireAccessTokenReason (server/middleware/tokenType.ts:98), and server/services/session-inactivity.ts:165 sessionLifetimeExceeded ends a token whose iat is from 2018. 4) The Neon project is still used: .github/c2c-agent.yml:16 `production_branch: 'ep-wild-forest-ahbojhu4-pooler'`, .devcontainer/devcontainer.json:17 NEON_PROD_BRANCH, and .github/workflows/neon-provisioning.yml:26-27 runs weekly. 5) .github/workflows/ci.yml:2451-2457 still only prints a ::warning that `$n` live credentials exist. 6) tests/ci/secret-history-scan.contract.test.ts:120 accepts only `live|public by design|not a secret`, and :128 requires the INF-22 block to say `live`, so recording a revocation would currently fail the contract. Nothing in the repo shows that any of the three was rotated.
records.fixedBy: 8fdfc74bd (.gitleaksignore:44-57): reclassifies only the HS256 VaultMarketingPage token as not a credential.
records.remaining: Three credentials are still recorded as live: the Neon owner passwords for ep-wild-forest-ahbojhu4 and ep-icy-brook-aha5br78, and the Hugging Face token. They are readable by anyone because the repository is still public. There is no founder decision on visibility. The CI step only warns, and the contract test has no way to record a revocation.
records.severityRationale: Kept at P0 because owner credentials for a live Neon project, which the repo itself calls the production branch and which CI still branches from weekly, are world-readable in a public repository. A design partner's security questionnaire will ask about exactly this. The fix takes the founder minutes in the Neon and Hugging Face consoles. Pilot data on AWS RDS is not directly exposed by these credentials, which is the only argument for a lower rating. It cannot be settled from the repo either way.
records.humanTestingNote: Testers will not see this. Note that any staging or test deployment pointed at the leaked Neon project puts tester data behind a publicly known owner password. Point human-testing environments at a database whose credentials have never been committed.
records.instructions:
1. Founder, in the Neon console for project ep-frosty-salad-afl93crk: reset the neondb_owner password for endpoint ep-wild-forest-ahbojhu4 and for ep-icy-brook-aha5br78. Then reset or delete every branch that inherited the old password: the agent and preview branches created by .github/workflows/neon-provisioning.yml, neon-preview-db.yml and .github/c2c-agent.yml. Update the NEON_* GitHub secrets and any local .env that used the old URIs.
2. Founder, at huggingface.co → Settings → Access Tokens: revoke the token committed in 3e1dcf8f0 (test-api-key.js:8, test-embeddings.js:7).
3. Prove each revocation by making it fail. From a secure machine, connect with the historical URI (`git show 8d5bce39c:AUTH_CREDENTIALS_LOCKED.md`, `git show f457478c8:_test_neon.cjs`; never paste the values anywhere) and expect `password authentication failed`. Call `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <old token>" https://huggingface.co/api/whoami-v2` and expect 401. Record the date and outcome only, never the values, under docs/evidence/.
4. On concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0: commit directly, merge rather than rebase), amend tests/ci/secret-history-scan.contract.test.ts. Line 120: accept `^# status: (live|revoked \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}|public by design|not a secret)`. Line 128: accept `live` or `revoked <date>` for the INF-22 block. Add a case asserting that a block saying `revoked` with no date is refused. Run that case against a scratch copy of the file and show it failing before you commit.
5. In the same commit, change the three `# status: live — revoke (founder; P0-17)` lines (.gitleaksignore:15, 31, 38) to `# status: revoked <YYYY-MM-DD>`. Add one reason line naming who revoked each credential and where the evidence is.
6. Make .github/workflows/ci.yml:2451-2457 (`Name the history credentials not yet revoked`) fail closed. Replace the `::warning` with `::error` plus `exit 1` when `n > 0`. First run that script locally against the current .gitleaksignore (n=3) and show it exits 1. Commit it in the same change as step 5, so the canonical branch never carries a red step for a known state.
7. Founder decision, recorded in docs/LAUNCH_DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md's decision log: make the repository private, or keep it public with written acceptance. If private, run `gh api repos/concept2cure/ClinicalSageAI-2-replit -X PATCH -f visibility=private`, then confirm `--jq .private` returns true. Plan for the CI-minutes cost (OPS-25) before switching.
8. Optional hardening: remove the endpoint names from .github/c2c-agent.yml:15-16 and .devcontainer/devcontainer.json:16-17, which advertise the leaked project as `production`.
records.acceptance: (a) Each old Neon owner password fails to authenticate against its endpoint, and the old Hugging Face token returns 401. Both results are recorded with dates, and no secret values appear in the evidence. (b) `grep -c '^# status: live' .gitleaksignore` returns 0. (c) The CI step `Name the history credentials not yet revoked` exits 1 when a `# status: live` block is present (shown failing on the pre-change file) and passes after the change. (d) tests/ci/secret-history-scan.contract.test.ts passes, and its new case refuses an undated `revoked` block (shown failing first). (e) A visibility decision is recorded. If the repository goes private, `gh api repos/concept2cure/ClinicalSageAI-2-replit --jq .private` returns true.
records.dependencies: Founder access to the Neon and Hugging Face consoles. OPS-25 (CI cost) if the repository is made private.

records.title: Still no AWS monitoring or alerting: no alarms, SNS topic or dashboards in terraform. Sentry is now configurable but optional and unset by default
records.evidenceAtHead: 1) `grep -rn 'aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm|aws_sns_topic|aws_cloudwatch_dashboard|aws_cloudwatch_log_metric_filter|aws_cloudwatch_composite_alarm' terraform/` returns 0 hits, and no workflow calls put-metric-alarm. 2) Sentry became plumbable after the audit (19d2be04a): terraform/stack/variables.tf:424-431 `sentry_dsn` defaults to "", terraform/stack/main.tf:338 adds SENTRY_DSN only when set, and terraform/environments/production/variables.tf:181-184 defaults to "". server/startup/env.ts:104-110 still only warns when SENTRY_DSN or REDIS_URL is missing. 3) There is no OTEL_* or METRICS_TOKEN anywhere in terraform/. 4) infra/alerts/background-jobs.yml and orchestrator.yml are Prometheus rules, and no Prometheus is deployed. 5) Container Insights is on (terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf:9), but nothing alarms on it. 6) docs/runbooks/ still holds the same 8 files (eCTD, ESG, corpus, env-var), with no incident, rollback or on-call runbook. docs/operations/database-disaster-recovery.md already existed at 92ccdba1, so the audit's 'no DR runbook' was partly wrong, but that does not change the alerting gap.
records.remaining: All of the fix remains: an SNS topic with subscribers, and alarms on ALB 5xx and target health, ECS running < desired, RDS CPU, storage, connections and memory, CloudFront 5xx, job-failure log lines and job staleness. Sentry must be made mandatory for production, and the incident, rollback and on-call runbooks must be written.
records.severityRationale: Outages, a failed nightly retention or audit-chain sweep, or a dead API task would go unseen until a pilot user reports them, so no SLA or Part 11 monitoring commitment is credible. This is not a safety blocker to starting, but it must be in place before pilot users rely on production.
records.humanTestingNote: Testers will not see this. During testing, failures are found only by testers or by someone reading server logs. Have someone watch the API logs and GET /api/health/background-jobs (server/startup/inline-endpoints.ts:222-255) during test sessions.
records.instructions:
1. Founder: name the alert destination (one or more email addresses, or a pager HTTPS endpoint) and create a Sentry project. Supply the DSN.
2. Add `aws_lb.this.arn_suffix` and `aws_lb_target_group.api.arn_suffix` outputs to terraform/modules/alb/outputs.tf. Add `api_log_group_name` (aws_cloudwatch_log_group.api.name, terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf:18) to terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/outputs.tf. Add `identifier` (aws_db_instance.this.identifier) to terraform/modules/rds/outputs.tf.
3. Create terraform/modules/monitoring/{main.tf,variables.tf,outputs.tf}. It needs: aws_sns_topic `alarms` with kms_master_key_id set; one aws_sns_topic_subscription per var.alarm_emails; and these aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm resources, each with alarm_actions and ok_actions pointing at the topic:
   (a) AWS/ApplicationELB HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count, Sum > 10 per 300 s, 2 of 2 datapoints.
   (b) AWS/ApplicationELB HTTPCode_ELB_5XX_Count, Sum > 5 per 300 s.
   (c) AWS/ApplicationELB HealthyHostCount, Minimum < var.api_desired_count for 3×60 s, treat_missing_data=breaching.
   (d) ECS/ContainerInsights RunningTaskCount for ClusterName and ServiceName (module.ecs.cluster_name, module.ecs.api_service_name), Minimum < var.api_desired_count for 5×60 s.
   (e) AWS/RDS: CPUUtilization > 80 for 3×300 s; FreeStorageSpace < 10 GiB; FreeableMemory < 256 MiB; DatabaseConnections > 80% of the instance's max_connections.
   (f) AWS/CloudFront 5xxErrorRate, Average > 5 for 2×300 s, dimensions DistributionId=module.cdn.distribution_id and Region=Global.
   (g) aws_cloudwatch_log_metric_filter on the API log group, matching the failure lines the code emits: `Scheduled retention sweep failed` (server/jobs/retentionCron.ts:410), `Audit chain integrity check failed` (server/jobs/auditChainIntegritySweep.ts:615), `External intelligence sweep crashed` (server/jobs/externalIntelligenceSweep.ts:52), and `security posture transitioned` together with `failing` (server/services/securityHealthScheduler.ts runOnce). Publish them as namespace C2C/Jobs, metric JobFailure. Alarm on Sum >= 1 per 300 s.
4. Job staleness. In server/db/scheduledOnce.ts runScheduledOncePerWindow, after the `UPDATE scheduled_job_claims SET finished_at` succeeds, write one CloudWatch EMF JSON line to stdout: `{"_aws":{"CloudWatchMetrics":[{"Namespace":"C2C/Jobs","Dimensions":[["JobName"]],"Metrics":[{"Name":"JobSucceeded"}]}]},"JobName":<jobName>,"JobSucceeded":1}`. The awslogs driver ships it. In the monitoring module, alarm on JobSucceeded Sum < 1 over period 86400 with treat_missing_data=breaching, for retention-sweep and audit-chain-integrity-sweep. Unit-test that the line is emitted only on success; show the test failing before the change.
5. Wire `module "monitoring"` into terraform/stack/main.tf after module "cdn" (around line 523). Add stack variable `alarm_emails` (list(string)) and pass it through environments/{production,staging}/main.tf and their variables.tf. In environments/production/variables.tf, add validations requiring length(alarm_emails) >= 1, and requiring sentry_dsn != "" on the existing variable at line 181.
6. Add SENTRY_DSN to the deploy preflight in .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml, next to the CLAMAV_HOST check (around line 715), so a production task definition without it is refused with ::error.
7. Add terraform/stack/tests/monitoring.tftest.hcl (mocked provider, like the existing tests). It asserts that every alarm above exists with the SNS topic in alarm_actions. Add a production run with alarm_emails=[] and a run with sentry_dsn="", both using expect_failures. Run them before adding the validations and show them failing. Add the file to .github/workflows/terraform-tests.yml.
8. Write docs/runbooks/incident-response.md (alarm → owner → first actions per alarm), docs/runbooks/rollback.md (redeploy the previous task-definition revision with `aws ecs update-service --task-definition <prev>`; migrations are forward-only under Rule 1) and an on-call rota.
9. In staging, set the API desired count to 0, or stop the task, and confirm the SNS email arrives within 5 minutes. Restore the service. Then force a job failure (for example ENABLE_RETENTION_SWEEP with a broken policy) and confirm the JobFailure alarm fires. File both results as evidence.
records.acceptance: (a) `terraform test` passes for the new monitoring tests. A production plan with no alarm_emails or an empty sentry_dsn is refused, and each refusal is shown failing before its validation was added. (b) deploy-aws.yml preflight refuses a task definition without SENTRY_DSN (shown on a doctored task-definition JSON). (c) In staging, stopping the API task pages the subscriber within 5 minutes. Blocking the DB security group drives HealthyHostCount below desired and pages. A forced retention or audit-sweep failure fires JobFailure. (d) A day with no retention-sweep success fires the staleness alarm (demonstrate by disabling the sweep in staging). (e) A thrown test error appears in Sentry.
records.dependencies: OPS-01 (a first real apply/deploy of staging), the founder's alert destination and Sentry DSN, and OPS-07 (job-claim rows, already present) for the staleness metric.

records.title: Scheduler duplication across replicas is fixed for every default-on job via Postgres lease plus per-window claim. Three opt-in jobs remain uncoordinated and no gate prevents regressions
records.evidenceAtHead: 1) New server/db/scheduledOnce.ts (03dbeaf51, 4b1583a2c, f0533ac96, all after 92ccdba1). runScheduledOnce takes a session-level `pg_try_advisory_lock($ns, hashtext(job))` (:82). runScheduledOncePerWindow adds a durable claim, `INSERT INTO scheduled_job_claims ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, with epoch-aligned windowKeyOf. The table is migrations/20261001d_scheduled_job_claims.sql (public, organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL, IF NOT EXISTS only), listed in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES at scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:3022. 2) Coordinated at HEAD: retention sweep (server/jobs/retentionCron.ts:409, default ON in production); external intelligence (externalIntelligenceSweep.ts:50, default ON); audit-chain sweep (auditChainIntegritySweep.ts:612); 5-minute chain monitor (services/audit/chainIntegrityMonitor.ts, per window); sentinel (services/sentinel/scheduler.ts:149); schedule-of-events (scheduleOfEventsSweep.ts:101 lease, plus a per-schedule guarded claim at :117); digest heartbeat (digest-heartbeat.ts:179 lease plus a DB per-day check); memory consolidation and citation pruner (lease). Task-due sweep stamps with a guarded UPDATE before notifying (taskDueSweep.ts:94-110). The submission-chat sweep is an idempotent UPDATE (submission-chat-proposal-store.ts:508). securityHealthScheduler is read-only and per-process by design. 3) tests/db/scheduled-once-lease.dbtest.ts:63 (two sessions run fn once) and scheduled-once-window.dbtest.ts:53,87 run in CI's db job (ci.yml:1550). 4) Still uncoordinated: server/jobs/driftSentinelSweep.ts:75 (setInterval), corpusIngestionSweep.ts:164 and regulatoryHorizonScan.ts:154 (cron.schedule). All three default OFF and none of their ENABLE_* flags is set anywhere in terraform/. 5) No ci:* gate or test enforces that a new scheduler goes through runScheduledOnce: grep of scripts/ci and tests/ci finds no reference.
records.fixedBy: 03dbeaf51, 4b1583a2c, f0533ac96: server/db/scheduledOnce.ts:72-190 and migrations/20261001d_scheduled_job_claims.sql. Call sites: server/jobs/retentionCron.ts:409, server/jobs/externalIntelligenceSweep.ts:50, server/jobs/auditChainIntegritySweep.ts:612, server/jobs/scheduleOfEventsSweep.ts:101, server/services/sentinel/scheduler.ts:149, server/services/digest/digest-heartbeat.ts:179, server/services/audit/chainIntegrityMonitor.ts, server/services/memory-consolidation-job.ts, server/services/ana/citation-run-pruner.ts.
records.remaining: Drift sentinel, corpus ingestion and the regulatory horizon scan would run once per process (three times in production) if their ENABLE_* flag were turned on. Nothing stops a future scheduler from being added without the lease.
records.severityRationale: Every scheduler that runs by default in production, which covers the Part 11 retention dispositions, audit sweeps, notifications and external fetches named in the finding, now runs once per window across tasks. The leftovers are opt-in jobs outside the launch catalog. They are off in the deployed configuration.
records.humanTestingNote: Testers will not see this. Local or staging runs one process, so duplication cannot occur there in any case.
records.instructions:
1. On concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0), wrap the three opt-in schedulers using the pattern in server/jobs/externalIntelligenceSweep.ts:49-53. (a) server/jobs/driftSentinelSweep.ts:75: replace the setInterval body with `void runScheduledOncePerWindow('drift-sentinel-sweep', windowKeyOf(intervalMs), () => runWithSystemTenantScope('drift-sentinel-sweep', () => runDriftSentinelSweep())).catch(...)`. If runDriftSentinelSweep already enters a scope, keep its scoping and drop the extra wrapper. (b) server/jobs/corpusIngestionSweep.ts:164: wrap runCorpusIngestionSweep() in `runScheduledOncePerWindow('corpus-ingestion-sweep', windowKeyOf(7 * DAY_MS), ...)`. (c) server/jobs/regulatoryHorizonScan.ts:154: wrap runRegulatoryHorizonScan() in `runScheduledOncePerWindow('regulatory-horizon-scan', windowKeyOf(7 * DAY_MS), ...)`. Import from '../db/scheduledOnce'.
2. Extend tests/db/scheduler-jobs-under-rls.dbtest.ts, using tests/db/scheduler-harness.ts. For each of the three jobs, set the ENABLE_* flag, stub the external fetchers, and run two concurrent ticks and then a later non-overlapping tick in the same window. Assert the job body ran exactly once. Run against the unwrapped code first and show the test failing.
3. Add scripts/ci/check-scheduler-lease.mjs. It scans server/**/*.ts (excluding __tests__) for `cron.schedule(` and for `setInterval(` in files under server/jobs/ or named *scheduler*, *sweep* or *heartbeat*. Each such file must reference runScheduledOnce or runScheduledOncePerWindow, or appear in scripts/ci/scheduler-lease-baseline.json with a written reason. Initial baseline entries: securityHealthScheduler.ts (per-process read-only posture check), taskDueSweep.ts (guarded UPDATE before notify), submission-chat-sweep-scheduler.ts (idempotent UPDATE), workers/ivdr-pack-worker.ts (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED). The script must refuse an entry with an empty reason. Add `ci:scheduler-lease` and `ci:scheduler-lease:selftest` to package.json. The selftest writes a temp file with an unwrapped cron.schedule under a fake server/jobs/ path and expects exit 1.
4. Wire `npm run ci:scheduler-lease` into .husky/pre-push and the Lint job in .github/workflows/ci.yml. Show it failing on HEAD before step 1 lands (the three files) and passing after.
records.acceptance: (a) The new dbtests run each of drift-sentinel, corpus-ingestion and regulatory-horizon exactly once for two concurrent ticks plus one later tick in the same window. They were shown failing against the pre-change code. (b) `npm run ci:scheduler-lease` exits 1 on the pre-change tree, naming the three files, and exits 0 after. `ci:scheduler-lease:selftest` passes, which proves the failure branch. (c) Existing tests/db/scheduled-once-*.dbtest.ts still pass in CI's db job.
records.dependencies: None. Related to OPS-08, where the worker would be a third process, and OPS-06 (job-staleness metric built on scheduled_job_claims).

records.title: Worker ECS service, task definition, log group and ECR repo are still declared with nothing to deploy. The example tfvars now sets 0, but the production variable still defaults to 1
records.evidenceAtHead: 1) terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf still declares the worker: log group at :24-28; aws_ecs_task_definition.worker at :281-315 with image=var.worker_image and no `command`, so it would run the image's CMD, meaning the API; aws_ecs_service.worker at :368-393, desired_count=var.worker_desired_count. 2) terraform/stack/main.tf:31 creates ECR repos ["api","worker"] (terraform/modules/ecr/variables.tf:9). :402 worker_image is `<worker repo>:<image_tag>`, a repo nothing pushes to. terraform/stack/outputs.tf:17 is ecr_worker_url. 3) terraform/environments/production/variables.tf:53-56 still defaults worker_desired_count to 1. terraform/environments/production/terraform.tfvars.example:47-50 changed from 1 at 92ccdba1 to 0, with a comment saying it stays 0 until a worker image exists and that keeping a worker is founder decision B6+B7. Staging defaults to 0. 4) .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml:34-67 still says no worker image exists and carries `TODO(infra)` to remove the service and repo from terraform. 5) The worker now carries the full boot contract (stack/main.tf:437-444; asserted in terraform/stack/tests/boot_contract.tftest.hcl:167-176). If the API image were pushed to the worker repo, a third API process would start; its schedulers are now coordinated by server/db/scheduledOnce.ts (see OPS-07), which removes the duplicate-sweep half of the impact.
records.fixedBy: terraform/environments/production/terraform.tfvars.example:47-50 (worker_desired_count = 0). The duplicate-scheduler consequence is mitigated by OPS-07's lease (03dbeaf51, 4b1583a2c).
records.remaining: The phantom service, task definition, log group and ECR repo all still exist. An apply that does not copy the example tfvars uses the production default of 1, and the service then tries forever to pull from an empty repo. The founder's B6+B7 decision on keeping a worker is still not taken.
records.severityRationale: The documented apply path (tfvars example) yields 0 tasks, and a third process would no longer duplicate sweeps. What remains is a misconfiguration trap, ECS noise and false alarms once OPS-06 alarms exist, plus dead infrastructure. It should be cleaned up before enterprise GA, not before the pilot.
records.humanTestingNote: Testers will not see this; it is AWS infrastructure only.
